meta.why: A consistent wind-down can support sleep for some people. It is an experiment, not a guarantee or a test of effort.

hero.title: Sleep Wind-Down Checklist
hero.subtitle: Choose a realistic routine
hero.description: Select a small number of changes that fit your life. If sleep problems are persistent, severe, or linked to another health concern, discuss them with an appropriate clinician.

tiles.title: **Environment options**
content: Use a temperature that feels comfortable
Reduce unwanted light or noise where practical
Reserve the bed for sleep when possible
Adapt pillows or positioning for comfort

tiles.title: **Wind-down options**
content: Dim lights if that feels helpful
Write down unfinished tasks for tomorrow
Use comfortable breathing rather than forcing a pattern

tiles.title: **Timing considerations**
content: Notice whether caffeine timing affects you
Avoid treating one universal cutoff as a rule
Consider how alcohol, meals, medication, and activity affect your sleep
Ask a clinician or pharmacist when health conditions or medication are involved

tiles.title: **Consistency without perfection**
content: A regular wake time can be useful
One difficult night is not failure
Change one or two things at a time
Judge patterns over several days rather than one morning

microAction.title: Tonight's Experiment
microAction.description: Choose one or two options to try for several nights. Record what you did and how rested or capable you felt the next day.
